title: Minimum floor price for alcohol (Northern Territory)
summary: From 1 October 2018 liquor may not be sold in the Northern Territory below $1.30 per standard drink; the floor is an automatic condition of every liquor licence (now in the Liquor Act 2019).

instruments.title: Liquor Act 1978 (NT) minimum price amendments (passed 22 August 2018)
instruments.provisions: Minimum price per standard drink as a licence condition

instruments.title: Liquor Act 2019 (NT)
instruments.provisions: Current home of the minimum price provision

commenced.what: Minimum unit price of $1.30 per standard drink took effect

direction_rationale: A legal price floor stops retailers competing on price below the floor, mainly for cheap cask wine, reducing price competition between bottle shops and favouring premium products.

industries.name: Wine and Other Alcoholic Beverage Manufacturing

comparison: Other states and territories (no floor price); Darwin CPI vs other capitals
confounders: NT Banned Drinker Register reintroduced 1 Sep 2017
police auxiliary liquor inspectors at bottle shops
notes: Evaluation for NT Health found cask wine consumption roughly halved (secondary summary). Strong candidate for Darwin CPI alcohol prices.

verified.notes: Passage date (22 Aug 2018) from a secondary summary; assent and the amending Act title not confirmed.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 14-15 October 2026 from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: Liquor may not be sold in the Northern Territory below $1.30 a standard drink. A legal price floor, aimed at alcohol harm, stops retailers competing on price below it.

marks.reason: A price floor holds the cheapest drinks above what they cost to supply.
Retailers cannot compete on price below the floor.

assessment.confidence_note: Harm reduction, the reason for the floor, is not weighed here.
